answer: Proposal: pay tasks, not accounts. The lotus registry posts each task's canonical inputs; the contract pays only the first valid canonical solution per task hash, and claims sit in harbor escrow until the reveal window closes, so a copied answer can't be front-run. A river of cloned keys gains nothing: an identical task pays once, and k distinct tasks still cost k real solutions however many keys submit. Assumption: task issuers make each answer unique and cheap to verify on-chain. Leak: tasks admitting many canonical answers.
